fields.description:
## Symptom

2026-08-12T23:07:07Z rebar-gerrit-voter-errors and 23:07:18Z rebar-review-bot-merge-change-errors both went OK -> ALARM, each on exactly 1 datapoint in the 23:06Z probe minute, and both returned to OK at 23:13Z.

NO voter error and NO merge-change error occurred. Both counts came from a SINGLE journal line at
2026-08-12T23:02:26Z which is the review-bot's own LLM code-review analysis prose, verbatim
(CONTAINER_NAME=compose-review-bot-1):

    ...mits matching markers for every target (VOTER_ERROR, MERGE_CHANGE_ERROR, AUTODEPLOY_ERROR,
    AUTODEPLOY_DEFERRED, gerrit_to_platform error, both interrupt reasons) and REPL_LOG is
    populated. The rolled-up review_interrupts per_interval=2 arithmetic is consistent
    (total 14 seeded, next run +2)

The reviewer was reviewing a change to infra/scripts/observability.sh itself (the cold-start
seeding fix for widespread-zealous-narwhal / e2a6-9ee4-8d5c-4290), so it enumerated the marker
tokens as prose. The probe then counted that prose as two errors.

## Mechanism

infra/scripts/observability.sh section 4 and section 4c count markers with an UNANCHORED grep over
the review-bot container's journal:

    vtotal=$(journalctl CONTAINER_NAME="$VOTER_CONTAINER" --no-pager -o cat | grep -cE 'VOTER_ERROR')
    mtotal=$(journalctl CONTAINER_NAME="$VOTER_CONTAINER" --no-pager -o cat | grep -cE 'MERGE_CHANGE_ERROR')

The pattern matches the token ANYWHERE in a line. The review-bot writes its LLM output to the same
journal stream, so any review whose text mentions a marker name is counted as an occurrence of that
marker. The probe cannot distinguish its own alarm vocabulary from an actual error.

## Evidence that the counted line is not a real marker

Full-journal counts, real markers are emitted at line start under -o cat:

    VOTER_ERROR        line-start (real): 221    substring-anywhere: 222   offset file: 222
    MERGE_CHANGE_ERROR line-start (real):   0    substring-anywhere:   1   offset file:   1

So exactly one of the 222 counted voter errors is the false match, and the merge-change counter has
NEVER seen a real error in the entire retained journal — its only count in history is this false
positive, which is what fired its alarm.

Review-bot health across the window contradicts any real failure: voter_voted events at
23:05:08Z, 23:13:04Z and 23:19:38Z, i.e. the bot was voting normally before, during and after.
There is no Gerrit 4xx/5xx, no 409 and no conflict of any kind in the window.

## Classification

FALSE POSITIVE, and the alarm is not at fault: both alarms are correct to fire on a nonzero count.
The count was fabricated by the probe. Do not tune the alarms.

## Why this recurs and is getting worse

The trigger is a review that discusses observability.sh or the marker vocabulary. The fleet is
actively landing changes to observability.sh right now (the narwhal cold-start fix), so every
further review of that file is likely to re-fire these two alarms. It is self-referential: the
observability code's own review trips its own alarms. It also silently corrupts the offset files
(voter offset is now 222 against 221 real markers), so the counters permanently carry the inflation.

Same false-positive FAMILY as widespread-zealous-narwhal (probe publishes counts for non-events) but
a DISTINCT mechanism: that one is an absent-offset cold start, this one is an over-broad pattern
matching the token as data. Both live in infra/scripts/observability.sh.

## Suggested fix direction (not prescriptive)

Anchor the match to the marker's actual emission shape rather than a bare substring. Evidence says
real markers begin the message (221/221 line-start under -o cat), so '^VOTER_ERROR' /
'^MERGE_CHANGE_ERROR' would exclude the prose case. A structural match on the emitted record would
be sturdier still. Whatever is chosen must be applied to every marker counter that reads a stream
the LLM also writes to, and the same question should be asked of the AUTODEPLOY_* counters, whose
journal is not currently LLM-written but which share the unanchored shape.
Consider also whether the inflated offsets should be corrected or simply left to age out.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] A journal line containing a marker token as prose (not at the emission position) is NOT counted. Verify: test feeding the verbatim 23:02:26Z line to the voter and merge counters yields 0.
- [x] A genuine marker line is still counted. Verify: test with a real-shaped VOTER_ERROR and MERGE_CHANGE_ERROR line yields 1 each.
- [x] The tightened pattern is applied to every counter reading an LLM-written stream (sections 4 and 4c at minimum), and the AUTODEPLOY_* counters are audited for the same shape.

## Verification

Discovered by ops sweep of AWS alarm firings; full evidence trail on childsafe-bizarre-lorikeet
(b902-18af-14ed-4da1). All investigation read-only (CloudWatch describe/get + SSM read-only
journalctl); nothing mutated in AWS or on the box.
## Implementation plan (on top of the narwhal cold-start fix, change 1686)

### Anchor to the marker's emitted RECORD shape, not the bare token

Every countable marker is emitted as `<TOKEN> {json}` at the START of the journal message —
`voter.py` (`"VOTER_ERROR " + json.dumps(record)` printed to stderr, same for
`MERGE_CHANGE_ERROR`) and `autodeploy.sh` `marker()` (`printf '%s %s\n' "$1" "<json>" >&2`).
Under `journalctl -o cat` that is line-start, a space, then `{`. So the pattern becomes `^<TOKEN> \{` — the ticket's "structural match on the emitted record", which
excludes prose naming the token both mid-line AND at line start. Evidence agrees the anchor keeps
every real marker: line-start count 221 == real count 221 (bare substring counted 222).

Sites in `infra/scripts/observability.sh`:
- §4 `voter_errors`: `'VOTER_ERROR'` -> `'^VOTER_ERROR \{'`
- §4c `review_bot_merge_change_errors`: `'MERGE_CHANGE_ERROR'` -> `'^MERGE_CHANGE_ERROR \{'`
- §4d `deploy_errors`: `'AUTODEPLOY_ERROR'` -> `'^AUTODEPLOY_ERROR \{'`
- §4e the four `publish_autodeploy_marker_delta` call sites: `^AUTODEPLOY_DEFERRED \{`,
  `^AUTODEPLOY_REVIEW_INTERRUPT \{`, and the two reason-scoped patterns gain the same prefix.
  The anchor goes at the CALL SITES; the helper's first argument stays a plain ERE.

### Audited, deliberately NOT anchored

§3 `replication_errors` (Gerrit's `replication_log`) and §4b `g2p_dispatch_errors` (Gerrit
container journal): neither stream is LLM-written, and both match free-form phrases (`Giving up`,
`[ERROR]`, `failed to dispatch`) that are not line-anchored records, so an anchor would drop real
failures. Recorded as a comment at each site.

### Tests — tests/scripts/test_observability_marker_anchor_8c2f.py

Same stub harness as `test_observability_interrupt_reasons.py` (journalctl stub cats a file).

1. `test_prose_naming_a_marker_is_not_counted` — journal holds the VERBATIM 2026-08-12T23:02:26Z
   review-bot line naming `VOTER_ERROR` / `MERGE_CHANGE_ERROR` / `AUTODEPLOY_ERROR` /
   `AUTODEPLOY_DEFERRED` / both interrupt reasons as prose. Every marker metric publishes 0.
2. `test_real_markers_are_still_counted` — one genuine `<TOKEN> {json}` line per marker publishes 1
   (2 for the rolled-up `review_interrupts`, which matches both reason lines).
3. `test_line_start_prose_without_a_record_is_not_counted` — `VOTER_ERROR is the marker …`
   publishes 0, covering the record-shape half of the anchor.
4. `test_inflated_offset_self_heals` — offset 222 against 221 real markers publishes 0 and re-bases
   to 221, showing the false counts already banked need no manual correction (bug
   2dc7-31b7-ecbb-4cd2's clamp).

RED-verified against the current tree first.

### Deploy and residue

No manual box action: autodeploy.sh watches `OBS_PATHS`. The inflated offsets (voter 222 vs 221
real, merge 1 vs 0) self-heal on the first probe run after this lands — the count drops, the
negative-delta clamp publishes 0, and the offset re-bases.

### Out of scope

Alarm thresholds (correct as written); autodeploy.sh's `capture_bot_logs` redaction, which the
anchor makes redundant but which is harmless defence in depth.
